title: Which organisations launched more rockets every year?
description: A graph of rocket launches by six organisations in three years is read in two steps, identify and infer. The video finds who rose every year and how SpaceX changed. Keeko thinks Rocket Lab rose every year because its last bar is the tallest.
teaching_notes: One idea: to say something rose every year, each bar must be taller than the one before. Watch for students who judge a rise from the last bar alone.

source: Worldwide rocket launches by organisations, three adjacent bars per organisation, scale 1 unit = 20 rockets; which organisations launched more rockets every year, and how SpaceX changed
video_script.why: The child can read a bar and its scale, and now reads a whole graph in two steps, identify and infer.
video_script.substitution: The book's own rocket launch graph, with the bar readings taken from the printed graph.
video_script.anchor: Rocket launches in three years by organisation, in order: SpaceX 31, 61, 96; Arianespace 15, 6, 3; ISRO 2, 5, 7; Galactic Energy 1, 2, 7; Rocket Lab 6, 6, 9; Expace 4, 4, 6. Scale 1 unit = 20 rockets.
video_script.wrong_move: Looks only at the tallest last bar and ignores that the first two bars are equal, so there was no rise in the first year.
video_script.payoff_line: SpaceX, ISRO and Galactic Energy launched more rockets every year.

final_answer.value: SpaceX, ISRO and Galactic Energy increased every year; SpaceX about doubled, then added about 35
final_answer.spoken: SpaceX, ISRO and Galactic Energy rose every year, and SpaceX about doubled and then added about thirty five

maths_rules: SpaceX 31, 61, 96: each bar taller than the one before, 61 is about 2 x 31, 96 - 61 = 35
Arianespace 15, 6, 3: each bar shorter, so it fell every year
ISRO 2, 5, 7 and Galactic Energy 1, 2, 7: each bar taller than the one before
Rocket Lab 6, 6, 9 and Expace 4, 4, 6: the first two bars are equal, so no rise in the first year
video_script.design: One idea: rising every year means each bar is taller than the one before. Six clusters of three bars sit in the anchor; on the board, arrows between neighbouring bars show a rise, a fall or no change.
open_questions: The bar readings for ISRO, Galactic Energy, Rocket Lab and Expace come from the worklist; the extracted book text gives only the SpaceX doubling, the SpaceX rise of about 35 and the Arianespace fall. Check the readings against the printed graph.
